title: The hostile environment
objective: Add the environment as actions (duplicate or late replies, expiry, crash and restart), find a hold that resolves twice, and fix it so that `res <= 1` holds with every environment action on.

choice.prompt: The provider's "ok" may arrive twice, or after the hold has expired. Which handler keeps `res <= 1`?

options.text: Resolve the hold if its stored state is still `capturing`, testing and writing in one step.
options.why: A compare-and-set on durable state turns duplicate and late replies into no-ops.

options.text: Remember each handled reply in the worker's memory, and skip any reply it has seen before.
options.why: A crash erases that memory, and the duplicate is handled again.

options.text: Check the stored state first, and write the result in a separate step that follows.
options.why: The check can go stale before the write, as in the double spend.

blocks.md:
Your system does not run alone. A model with only your actions assumes a polite world, so add the world as actions the scheduler may pick at any time. A reply arrives at least once, so it can arrive twice or after the hold has expired: replies stay in a message set, and one can be handled twice. Expiry is a competing path that releases a hold nobody captured. A crash erases the worker's memory but not the stored hold, and a restart brings the worker back.

With those on, the lifecycle can resolve twice if handling a reply and expiring a hold are each a read followed by a write that trusts the read. Both read `capturing`, then both write.

blocks.direction: Scene: the system's actions and the environment's side by side in the bar. Drive the hold with `Reply`, `Crash`, `Restart` and the expiry job, and watch `res`.

code.text:
---- MODULE HoldsUnsafe ----
EXTENDS HoldsEnv  \* read-only: Reply, Crash, TypeOK, NeverTwice
VARIABLES wseen, eseen  \* what the worker and the expiry job last read
vars == <<hst, tries, msgs, sent, up, res, wseen, eseen>>

Init == /\ hst = "available" /\ tries = 0 /\ msgs = {} /\ sent = FALSE
        /\ up = TRUE /\ res = 0 /\ wseen = "none" /\ eseen = "none"

Place == /\ hst = "available" /\ hst' = "held"
         /\ UNCHANGED <<tries, msgs, sent, up, res, wseen, eseen>>

Dispatch == /\ hst = "held" /\ tries < MaxTries /\ up
            /\ hst' = "capturing" /\ tries' = tries + 1 /\ sent' = TRUE
            /\ UNCHANGED <<msgs, up, res, wseen, eseen>>

HandleRead(r) == /\ r \in msgs /\ up /\ hst = "capturing" /\ wseen = "none"
                 /\ wseen' = r
                 /\ UNCHANGED <<hst, tries, msgs, sent, up, res, eseen>>

HandleWrite == /\ up /\ wseen /= "none"
               /\ hst' = IF wseen = "ok" THEN "captured" ELSE "held"
               /\ res' = IF wseen = "ok" THEN res + 1 ELSE res
               /\ wseen' = "none"
               /\ UNCHANGED <<tries, msgs, sent, up, eseen>>

ExpireRead == /\ eseen = "none" /\ hst \in {"held", "capturing"}
              /\ eseen' = hst
              /\ UNCHANGED <<hst, tries, msgs, sent, up, res, wseen>>

ExpireWrite == /\ eseen /= "none"
               /\ hst' = "released" /\ res' = res + 1 /\ eseen' = "none"
               /\ UNCHANGED <<tries, msgs, sent, up, wseen>>

Restart == /\ ~up /\ up' = TRUE
           /\ UNCHANGED <<hst, tries, msgs, sent, res, wseen, eseen>>

Next == \/ Place \/ Dispatch \/ \E r \in Replies : HandleRead(r)
        \/ HandleWrite \/ ExpireRead \/ ExpireWrite \/ Restart
        \/ \E r \in Replies : Reply(r) /\ UNCHANGED <<wseen, eseen>>
        \/ Crash /\ wseen' = "none" /\ UNCHANGED eseen
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
====
\* MaxTries = 2, CrashesOn = TRUE, INVARIANT NeverTwice

call.prompt: With duplicates, late replies, crashes and expiry all on, can this variant reach `res = 2`?

options.why: The worker and the expiry job both read `capturing`, then both write. Each path trusts a read the other invalidates.

options.text: No: each path checks the state before it writes.
options.why: Checking and writing in separate steps is the double spend again.

options.text: Only if the provider misbehaves on purpose.
options.why: Duplicates, delays and crashes are ordinary behavior for a network and a process.

blocks.after: TLC's own trace for this variant is the run {{run:RUN-tlc-resolved-twice}}. The fix makes each resolution one compare-and-set action on the stored state. With every environment action on and crashes on, TLC then finishes with no error, and both outcomes are reachable {{run:RUN-tlc-never-twice}}.

blocks.md:
The fixed actions test and write in one step:

```tla
Handle(r) == /\ r \in msgs /\ up /\ hst = "capturing"
             /\ hst' = IF r = "ok" THEN "captured" ELSE "held"
             /\ res' = IF r = "ok" THEN res + 1 ELSE res
             /\ UNCHANGED <<tries, msgs, sent, up>>

Expire == /\ hst = "held" /\ hst' = "released" /\ res' = res + 1
          /\ UNCHANGED <<tries, msgs, sent, up>>
```

Your claim CL-5.2 is drafted from that run, with one assumption dashed. This model sends the provider request in the same step that commits the hold, which a real system cannot do. That is SEAM-4, and a later stage takes the step apart.

choice.prompt: TLC's trace for the unsafe variant ends with `NeverTwice` violated: `Place`, `Dispatch`, `ExpireRead`, `Reply("ok")`, `HandleRead("ok")`, `HandleWrite`, `ExpireWrite` {{run:RUN-tlc-resolved-twice}}. Which class of witness is it?

options.text: A duplicate reply handled again after a crash.
options.why: No crash and no duplicate appear in the trace. One reply is handled once.

options.text: Two different resolvers, each trusting a read the other invalidates.
options.why: The worker and the expiry job both read `capturing`, and each write undoes the other's assumption.

options.text: One resolver whose own read went stale, with nothing else resolving.
options.why: Two resolvers write here. Either one alone would have kept `res` at 1.

choice.prompt: `res <= 1` is checked with every environment action on, crashes included. Which statement is true?

options.text: If it holds with crashes off, it holds with crashes on.
options.why: Adding actions adds behaviors, and one of them can break it.

options.text: If it holds, the provider charged at most once.
options.why: `res` counts resolutions in your model. The provider's ledger is not in it, and SEAM-4 is the gap.

options.text: If it holds with crashes on, it holds with crashes off.
options.why: Switching crashes off only removes behaviors, so a property of all behaviors survives it.

blocks.title: 2015: a transfer confirmed twice
blocks.md: In 2015 a researcher sent two near-simultaneous confirmations of the same staged gift-card transfer. Both went through, and $15 spread over three cards became $20 (Sakurity, 2015-05-21; [the write-up](https://sakurity.com/blog/2015/05/21/starbucks.html)). The toy model has each confirmation check the source card, then debit it from the value it read, while the credit is an atomic increment: {{run:RUN-tlc-starbucks15}}.

blocks.md: Learn TLA+ by Hillel Wayne, read 2026-10-23. Core › Nondeterminism (`core/nondeterminism.html`). Core › Temporal Properties, section "Anything can crash" (`core/temporal-logic.html#anything-can-crash`). Both are at [learntla.com](https://learntla.com/).
